definition: establish so firmly that change becomes difficult
memoryTip: Dig a trench and stay put — hard to dig out later.
correctPassage: Long-running subsidies can entrench wasteful habits if never reviewed.
wrongPassages: Volunteers will entrench the park by clearing litter every weekend.
The chef hoped to entrench the sauce by thinning it with water.
Editors entrench articles so readers finish them in under a minute.

definition: lay down as a rule; authorize a treatment
memoryTip: Pre-scribe: write the rule or medicine ahead of time.
correctPassage: The guidelines prescribe at least thirty minutes of activity each day.
wrongPassages: Mechanics prescribe oil changes by forbidding any maintenance at all.
Doctors prescribe rest by ordering nonstop marathon training.
She packed a spare prescribe in the trunk next to the tire.

definition: noticeable in an unwelcome or intrusive way
memoryTip: Ob-trude: sticks out where it doesn’t belong.
correctPassage: An obtrusive logo on the cover pulled attention from the photograph.
wrongPassages: The spy stayed obtrusive by wearing gray and avoiding eye contact.
Her obtrusive handwriting was so faint that graders needed a lamp.
They designed an obtrusive interface that hid every button until needed.

definition: having a mysterious or obscure meaning
memoryTip: Like a cryptogram — meaning locked behind a code.
correctPassage: The note was so cryptic that no one could decode its intent.
wrongPassages: Her cryptic instructions listed every step in numbered order.
The map was cryptic, with bold labels on every street and landmark.
He gave a cryptic speech that left no room for another interpretation.

definition: fill up again; restore a supply
memoryTip: Re-plenish: make full again after something is used up.
correctPassage: Heavy rains helped replenish the reservoirs after a dry summer.
wrongPassages: The editor will replenish the article by cutting half its length.
They hope to replenish traffic by closing two of the three lanes.
She replenished the debt by borrowing even more from the bank.
